title: The famous origin story is shaky. Murphy's law is said to come from a 1949 rocket sled test.
description:
Murphy's law is said to come from a 1949 rocket sled test. Historians call that link "by no means secure".

Sensors on a test harness read zero because some were wired backwards. Engineer Edward Murphy had proposed them for John Stapp's project.

Mathematician. Wrote that whatever can happen will happen, given enough trials.

No use of "Murphy's law" has been found before 1951. Accounts of who coined it conflict.

Even the law about things going wrong has an origin that went wrong.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murphy%27s_law (read): established that John Stapp ran project MX981 at Muroc Army Air Field in 1948 to 1949, that Edward Murphy proposed strain gauges on Stapp's harness, that in a trial reportedly around June 1949 the sensors read zero because some were wired backwards, that no one can reliably say who coined the phrase, that the link to Muroc is "by no means secure", that no use of "Murphy's law" has been found before 1951, that De Morgan wrote a similar idea in 1866, and that Stapp, Murphy and Nichols shared the 2003 Ig Nobel Prize "for (probably) giving birth to the name".
